title: Polynomial exterior evaluation and the signed derived cup map
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], $G$ a profinite group, and $r\geq0$. Use internal modules, trivial $G$-actions, ordinary derived categories, and the universe convention [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, def-sfb-condensed-action-module, def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-size-convention]. Fix additive condensed-group maps $a_i:\underline G\to(A,+)$, $1\leq i\leq r$. Write $C=R\Gamma_{A,G}(A[0])$, and let $\alpha_i=[a_i]:A[-1]\to C$ and the unital derived cup product have the positive connecting-class normalization of [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus].

Let $P^n$ be the internal direct sum of $A$ on monomials in $x_{a,i}$ for $1\leq a\leq n$, $1\leq i\leq r$, with polynomial notation [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] and differential
$$(df)(x_1,\ldots,x_{n+1})=f(x_2,\ldots,x_{n+1})+\sum_{a=1}^{n}(-1)^a f(x_1,\ldots,x_a+x_{a+1},\ldots,x_{n+1})+(-1)^{n+1}f(x_1,\ldots,x_n).$$
Set $K=\bigoplus_{I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,r\}}A[-|I|]$ with zero differential. Define $i:K\to P$ by $e_\varnothing\mapsto1$ and $e_{\{i_1<\cdots<i_q\}}\mapsto x_{1,i_1}\cdots x_{q,i_q}$. Evaluation $x_{a,i}\mapsto a_i(g_a)$ gives $\mathrm{ev}:P\to U^\bullet$, where $U^n=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(A[\underline G^n],A)$. Let $j:U^\bullet\to\mathscr B$ and $\epsilon:C\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathscr B$ be the canonical underived-to-derived map and normalized augmentation into the derived internal bar totalization of [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-invariant-bar]. Put $\eta=j\mathrm{ev}$.

Define $\chi:K\to C$ by the unit on the empty summand and $\alpha_{i_1}\smile\cdots\smile\alpha_{i_q}$ on the summand for $\{i_1<\cdots<i_q\}$. There exist signs $\varepsilon_q\in\{1,-1\}$ depending only on $q$ and the fixed tensor/shift convention, with $\varepsilon_0=\varepsilon_1=1$, such that the diagonal automorphism $\sigma$ of $K$ equal to $\varepsilon_{|I|}$ on its $I$-summand satisfies
$$\sigma^2=1,\qquad \eta i=\epsilon\chi\sigma$$
in $D(\operatorname{Mod}_A)$. On the empty summand this is equality with the actual cup unit. The assertion includes $r=0$, the zero ring and zero or repeated characters, and asserts equality of derived arrows, without asserting that $\eta$ is invertible or that $U^n$ is acyclic.

proof.text: All polynomial substitutions are $A$-linear maps on the monomial direct sums: each monomial expands into finitely many monomials. The evaluation formula of [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], applied on every profinite test object, is natural under restriction and gives the internal map $\mathrm{ev}$. The polynomial faces satisfy the cosimplicial identities: deleting end variables and replacing adjacent variables by their sum commute in the required order, with overlapping replacements using $(x+y)+z=x+(y+z)$. Thus terms in $d^2$ cancel in pairs with opposite signs. The faces on $U^\bullet$ are precisely those of [def-sfb-condensed-equivariant-bar-data]. Additivity $a_i(gh)=a_i(g)+a_i(h)$ identifies evaluation of each polynomial face with the corresponding group-bar face, including the two end faces because the action is trivial. Hence $\mathrm{ev}$ is a cochain map.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image; agent polynomial-bar normalization: polynomial chain maps, existing ordered-cup comparison, and finite-summand assembly.

proof.text: For $I=\{i_1<\cdots<i_q\}$ put $m_I=\prod_{b=1}^q x_{b,i_b}$. For $q\geq1$, in degree $q+1$ define $T_k=(\prod_{b<k}x_{b,i_b})(\prod_{b\geq k}x_{b+1,i_b})$ for $1\leq k\leq q+1$. The first face of $m_I$ is $T_1$, its $a$-th interior face is $T_a+T_{a+1}$, and its last face is $T_{q+1}$. Consequently $dm_I=T_1+\sum_{a=1}^q(-1)^a(T_a+T_{a+1})+(-1)^{q+1}T_{q+1}=0$, by cancellation of each $T_k$. For $q=0$, $d1=1-1=0$. These identities prove that the specified $i:K\to P$ is a cochain map. Its evaluated component on the $I$-summand is exactly $z_I(g_1,\ldots,g_q)=\prod_{b=1}^q a_{i_b}(g_b)$, and is $1$ for the empty summand.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image; agent polynomial-bar normalization: polynomial chain maps, existing ordered-cup comparison, and finite-summand assembly.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-internal-bar-ordered-cup] to the ordered tuple $(a_{i_1},\ldots,a_{i_q})$. Its $A,G,U^\bullet,\mathscr B,j,\epsilon$ and positive connecting classes are exactly those fixed here. It gives $j\mathrm{ev}i\iota_I=\varepsilon_q\epsilon(\alpha_{i_1}\smile\cdots\smile\alpha_{i_q})$, as derived arrows from $A[-q]$, where $\iota_I$ is the summand injection. That node explicitly makes $\varepsilon_q$ independent of the ring, group and characters, so the same degree sign works simultaneously for all subsets of size $q$. It also gives $\varepsilon_0=\varepsilon_1=1$, with the actual unit at $q=0$. No invertibility of $j$ or underived-column acyclicity enters this application.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image; agent polynomial-bar normalization: polynomial chain maps, existing ordered-cup comparison, and finite-summand assembly.

proof.text: Define $\sigma$ diagonally by these degree signs (degrees greater than $r$ have no summands). Since $\varepsilon_q^2=1$, its square is $1_K$. By the definition of $\chi$, step 3 says that $\eta i$ and $\epsilon\chi\sigma$ agree after every $\iota_I$. For the finite direct sum, writing $\pi_I$ for its projections, $1_K=\sum_I\iota_I\pi_I$; composing with this identity proves equality of the entire derived arrows. For $r=0$ there is only the empty summand and step 3 gives the unit equality. All polynomial cancellations and diagonal identities hold in the zero ring and in characteristic two. The cited comparison allows zero and repeated characters; nothing in the argument divides by a coefficient or asserts that their products are linearly independent.
